# ISHAVASYAM.ORG | SPACE STATION

> ISHAVASYAM.ORG is a Space Station research and engineering initiative. Its mission is to develop the capability to research, design and engineer a complete space station from first principles — advancing the systems, technologies and experimental research required for future human space infrastructure.

Research · Engineering · Experimentation

## Key facts

- What it is: a Space Station research and engineering initiative (a research platform, not an incorporated space company).
- Mission: develop the capability to research, design and engineer a complete space station from first principles.
- Research frontiers: station architecture; autonomous systems and station health; power and energy; life support; avionics and communications; robotics and operations.
- Current research emphasis: autonomous systems and station health (telemetry intelligence, anomaly detection, fault isolation, degradation prediction, safe-mode management and supervised autonomous recovery).
- Current work: digital research — architecture studies, subsystem models and simulation.
- Research lab: an ISHAVASYAM.ORG Space Station Research Lab is planned. It does not yet exist and is not operational.
- Intended collaborators: PhD and postdoctoral researchers, space scientists, senior engineers, principal engineers, chief architects, CTOs, research institutions and space-industry experts.
- Organisational context: an initiative of iTelematics Software Private Limited, Bangalore, India.
- The station shown on the website is an original conceptual architecture for illustration. It is not an engineered, approved or built design.
- ISHAVASYAM.ORG does not claim affiliation with, or endorsement by, any government space agency or space programme.

## About the name

"Ishavasyam" comes from the first mantra of the Isha Upanishad and may be understood as "all existence is pervaded by the Divine." The name has a philosophical foundation; the engineering programme itself is evidence-driven scientific research. Philosophical interpretations are kept distinct from scientific claims.
